findings.observation: Operator reports that pages and views are too noisy. This is accepted ground truth, not a hypothesis to falsify.
findings.consequence: The renewal must materially improve visual hierarchy rather than merely repaint the same density.
findings.recommendation: Each of the five directions must decide a primary task for every view, reduce competing controls/labels and retain purposeful fun rather than strip the game bare.
findings.verify: Main: capture representative existing surfaces to localize contributors, then compare redesigned hierarchy; do not ask screenshots to disprove the operator.

findings.observation: Operator reports that components are ugly.
findings.consequence: Token-only changes without new component craft will not satisfy the brief.
findings.recommendation: Reconsider shape, states, affordances, iconography, avatar language and composition across every actual component ID; include loading/error/empty states.
findings.verify: Main: inspect all shared primitives and their real compositions in five directions, not isolated button swatches only.

findings.observation: Operator reports that animations are awkward or missing.
findings.consequence: Both noisy effects and missing transition meaning need attention; adding more animation everywhere is not the answer.
findings.recommendation: Give each meaningful action/phase change one clear response and specify timing, interruption, reduced-motion and silent alternatives per motion ID.
findings.verify: Main: record start/join, valid-word threshold, submit/wait, reveal/Done, heart/crown, rematch and recovery transitions.

findings.observation: Operator reports text that is too big or too small.
findings.consequence: Existing nominal type classes cannot be treated as a validated hierarchy.
findings.recommendation: Establish role-based type sizes for handheld play, reading, shared-screen presentation and utility information; use real long human content.
findings.verify: Main: compare computed type sizes and readability at narrow widths, shared-display distance and 200% text.

findings.observation: Operator reports spacing is wrong.
findings.consequence: Preserving current whitespace laws mechanically would contradict the request.
findings.recommendation: Recompose spacing around related tasks and responsive constraints rather than uniformly increasing or decreasing padding.
findings.verify: Main: inspect content-to-action distance, scroll depth, textarea/keyboard geometry and actual vertical rhythm.

findings.observation: Operator explicitly reopens logo, typography, colors/themes, avatars/images/sounds, view flows/workflows and historical DESIGN.md identity/layout constraints. Requires five whole-product directions and treatment of every view/component/composition/animation.
findings.consequence: Existing Ink & Anticipation rules are historical source context, not mandatory visual acceptance criteria.
findings.recommendation: Preserve core mechanics, privacy, human attribution, guest access, mobile and accessibility obligations only; allow five genuinely different identities.
findings.verify: Main: reject any direction that keeps historical aesthetics solely because code comments call them laws.

findings.observation: Operator wants fun, whimsy and delight grounded in proven game principles, with simplicity/elegance but not austerity, Spartan or business-app styling.
findings.consequence: Noise reduction must not erase the social surprise and pleasure of the game.
findings.recommendation: Concentrate delight at meaningful group moments, playful identity and authored artifacts; keep utilitarian repair states calm and clear.
findings.verify: Main: evaluate emotional distinction during complete gameplay, not just marketing screenshots.

findings.observation: Source fixes the nine word targets, hidden carried-line writing, current-game matrix fairness for late joiners, soft timer, human reading and explicit share activation. These are independent of paper/seal/editorial styling.
findings.consequence: Conflating mechanics with current visual metaphors would constrain exploration unnecessarily, while casually changing them would exceed scope.
findings.recommendation: Keep the same state machine and permissions beneath new compositions; treat every alternate flow as presentation of existing actions, not new scoring, AI authorship, line skipping or voting rules.
findings.verify: Main: exercise nine rounds, late join, reveal authority and canceled/private sharing in the isolated local runtime.

findings.observation: Tailwind text tokens are rebound to a custom scale (lg 1.333rem, xl 1.777rem, 3xl 3.157rem, 5xl 5.61rem), while templates also use larger stock classes, clamp values and arbitrary pixel sizes.
findings.consequence: Source class names can hide unexpectedly large jumps; identical nominal roles have several sizing systems. Actual resulting sizes require compiled/browser evidence.
findings.recommendation: Use one explicit role scale per responsive context; reserve truly huge type for the projected stage or a deliberate hero, not routine status and form copy.
findings.verify: Main: collect computed font-size/line-height for home title, host/join title, waiting heading, textarea, buttons, help body and metadata at 320/390/768/1440px.

findings.observation: Tracked uppercase mono labels, numbered poem metadata, borders, chips and dividers repeat across chrome, cards and footers; several labels use 10px or smaller values.
findings.consequence: Likely contributors to the reported noise and too-small secondary text; labels can consume more attention and width than their information earns.
findings.recommendation: Prefer sentence case and grouped human-readable information; retain numbers only for meaningful round/reading order and keep accessible state labels explicit.
findings.verify: Main: count competing labels in lobby/reveal/recap screenshots and inspect at text zoom; this source observation is not a rendered contrast verdict.

findings.observation: The app combines global grain, offset accent shadows, repeated thin borders, blurred translucent trays and local accent tints; 404 adds its own grain/blur.
findings.consequence: Many material cues can compete with human poem content even when each is individually subtle.
findings.recommendation: Each direction should select one coherent depth/material grammar and use stronger treatment only for state or primary action. Texture is optional, not part of the mechanics.
findings.verify: Main: inspect light/dark screenshots on ordinary and high-density displays, including flat areas and body copy over texture.

findings.observation: Lobby and room chrome reference --radius-xl, but the inspected design token tables define sm/md/lg/full and no xl.
findings.consequence: Intended grouping shapes may silently resolve differently than designers assume; current class names alone cannot certify radius.
findings.recommendation: Choose a complete role-based shape system and remove unowned token references during the selected implementation, rather than preserve accidental fallback geometry.
findings.verify: Main: inspect computed border-radius on lobby panels/chrome; inventory is source-grounded and does not assert current pixels.

findings.observation: Room identity appears in chrome and a large room-code card; player quantity appears as readiness copy, seats, roster count and start-button requirement; join QR is available through both chrome and tools.
findings.consequence: Duplicated navigation/status may contribute to noise and reduce space for names/readiness.
findings.recommendation: Explore one dominant shared code/readiness composition and quieter optional tools, while keeping QR/code/share reachable and 2–8-player readiness visible.
findings.verify: Main: inspect host and nonhost lobbies with 1, 2 and 8 players, tools open, longest names and text zoom.

findings.observation: Host uses a left-aligned scroll frame and persistent action zone; Join uses a right-aligned title/card and ordinary page flow. Labels vary among Host Identity, Your Name, Session, Room and Game.
findings.consequence: People moving between create/join may have to relearn alignment, vocabulary and where the main action lives.
findings.recommendation: Use coherent naming and entry geometry unless a direction has a deliberate task-based reason to differ; keep invite-prefilled code and name focus behavior.
findings.verify: Main: walk home→host and home/invite→join on real mobile keyboard surfaces and compare action reachability.

findings.observation: Desktop writing uses min-height 320/360px textarea, large type, md spacing up to 64px between related blocks and an 80px submit button. The carried line and a large editable line share the same display-font language.
findings.consequence: Likely contributors to excessive empty space and weak received-versus-authored hierarchy, especially for the one-word rounds; mobile has a separate compressed rhythm.
findings.recommendation: Design carried context, input and constraint as one deliberate task unit with proportional spacing; make word-one and word-five rounds both feel intentional without inflating short content.
findings.verify: Main: screenshot blank, one-word, five-word and longest-valid lines; inspect distance to slots and Submit before/after keyboard opening.

findings.observation: Several phases use clipped viewport frames with separately scrollable body/action zones; WaitingScreen nests another full-height scroll area and min-h-full headline block.
findings.consequence: Functional anti-keyboard-overlap work can create awkward nested scroll, unreachable content or large empty stretches; source alone cannot determine the rendered result.
findings.recommendation: Keep main action in a reachable in-flow tray but minimize independent scroll regions and give the primary task a simple reading order. Preserve safe areas and VisualViewport handling.
findings.verify: Main: actual phone keyboard, landscape, 200% text, short viewport, long errors and open menu; inspect scroll chaining and focused element visibility.

findings.observation: Filled chips use whitespace-nowrap and grow to the whole word; overflow-x is hidden on writing containers. Inputs allow up to 500 characters and word targets count whitespace, not character width.
findings.consequence: A single extremely long human token can be wider than the phone, and source containment may clip the constraint representation; not a rendered claim.
findings.recommendation: Give long words a legible wrap strategy within the selected direction while preserving exact text and whitespace tokenization. Keep over-target status readable without flooding chips.
findings.verify: Main: use ordinary long words and a boundary-length unbroken token in local writing; inspect chips, textarea, target status and action tray at 320px.

findings.observation: Help describes squares filling and sealing a line, while the active writer supplies text chips containing words and labels the action Submit.
findings.consequence: A new player may look for an outdated visual cue or different action name.
findings.recommendation: Align help examples, coachmark, live constraint and action verb to the selected direction; retain exact target counts and blind collaboration.
findings.verify: Main: first-use play without prior product knowledge; compare the help description to the live valid/overflow states.

findings.observation: Writing requests placeholder:text-text-muted/20 but global ::placeholder forces muted color/opacity; disabled buttons combine grayscale and brightness changes; contrast contract covers flat token pairs, not every alpha/filter composition.
findings.consequence: Computed placeholder and disabled contrast can differ from token-table expectations; color-only state emphasis may be ambiguous.
findings.recommendation: Check actual composited colors for all states and use form labels/text/state shape alongside color. Keep essential placeholder/instructions on a readable floor.
findings.verify: Main: inspect computed placeholder/disabled values and rendered contrast in both modes, including ready/not-ready states and translucent trays.

findings.observation: Clock is a decorative 2px shrinking line, last-quarter accent, then full-width low-opacity line on overtime; it is aria-hidden and never gates submission.
findings.consequence: People may interpret the reset-to-full bar as time renewed or miss the pacing cue entirely; motion/sensory changes must not turn it into a punitive countdown.
findings.recommendation: Choose a clearer but still gentle pacing vocabulary and make the absence of a hard deadline apparent without adding new gameplay timing rules.
findings.verify: Main: watch 90-second normal→warm→overtime transition in both motion modes with active and waiting users.

findings.observation: Waiting repeats progress in headline/count/segments/names/avatar treatments; submitted names become struck through, while away and watching markers use small text and multiple opacity reductions.
findings.consequence: A fulfilled social contribution can read as crossed-out/absent, and status differences may blur on small screens.
findings.recommendation: Give contributed/writing/away/watching distinct positive, understandable states with one primary progress signal; retain names and privacy rather than hide uncertainty behind ambient animation.
findings.verify: Main: compare 2/8-player waiting, mixed away/spectators and all-ready moments on handheld and shared screens.

findings.area: Leavers, fallback readers and host migration
findings.observation: Presence heartbeats run every 15s; away threshold is 45s and stale-host threshold 60s. Frontend reacts to isHost and fallback-reader authority but has no distinct host-handoff notice.
findings.consequence: A new host or fallback reader can acquire responsibility without an obvious explanation; a briefly absent person and a leaver can look similar.
findings.recommendation: Design role transitions and step-in copy within existing server authority; keep the group moving without adding voting/ownership mechanics.
findings.verify: Main: simulate host absence and reader fallback only locally, then inspect newly available controls, status language and assistive announcements.

findings.observation: Late join gets no current assignment and sees You are watching this game; next-game promise is in WaitingScreen. Spectators count as room people but are excluded from round completion.
findings.consequence: A redesign focused only on writer screens could leave real joiners confused or accidentally change fairness by assigning retroactive work.
findings.recommendation: Provide a clear low-noise spectator identity, current-phase orientation and promise of the next existing game; do not expose hidden text or add side activities/mechanics.
findings.verify: Main: join during a middle round, watch through reveal and participate in rematch; inspect every transition.

findings.observation: Closing the lobby removes participant rows; getRoomState null also represents wrong/expired code, no identity or no membership. UI currently calls all of these Room not found.
findings.consequence: A person whose host closed the room may receive an explanation that blames their code, while designs could mistakenly invent a distinct CLOSED component.
findings.recommendation: Explore access-safe context and clear return/join actions while acknowledging the current shared branch; any differentiated explanation must respect data the client actually has.
findings.verify: Main: close a local lobby with a second browser present, then revisit as leaver/nonmember and inspect state/copy without remote gameplay.

findings.area: Lobby start, close and leave feedback
findings.observation: Start/leave/close actions await mutations but the component has no submitting/pending state; close/leave are immediately invoked by buttons.
findings.consequence: An action can feel unacknowledged during delay and the destructive scope of Close room is easy to miss beside ordinary navigation.
findings.recommendation: Specify disabled/busy and consequence-aware presentation for the existing actions in each direction; do not invent new termination rules.
findings.verify: Main: inspect slow local mutation responses and compare host Close room with participant Leave room labels/feedback.

findings.observation: Reading-circle Read status is driven by isRevealed, while the reader presses Reveal & Read before reading the displayed poem. Reading now is first unrevealed, not a transmitted start/finish performance state.
findings.consequence: The board can imply a reading is complete or a different person is reading while a poem is still being read aloud.
findings.recommendation: Use labels and visual hierarchy faithful to available revealed/assigned state, and differentiate stage-local Finish from shared reveal status. Do not add a new synchronization mechanic as a visual fix.
findings.verify: Main: keep one poem open on reader while observing another device; record circle labels before reveal, during aloud reading, after Done and during reread.

findings.observation: All-revealed recap is appended below assignment/reread/presentation/reading-circle content. Poem overlay footer offers heart, sharing, save and Done; recap offers share, rematch, lobby and exit.
findings.consequence: The group’s next social action may compete with archival/publishing utilities, and recap can be below a substantial scroll stack.
findings.recommendation: Separate the primary read/continue rhythm from optional keeping/sharing, with a clearly visible completion moment using existing actions and no forced publication.
findings.verify: Main: finish the last poem on phone and desktop, close it and locate recap/rematch without hunting; compare primary versus secondary visual weight.

findings.observation: Avatar sizes range 8–20px even when stage names become many rem tall; palette collision resolution is room-relative and compact contributor dots show generic titles rather than names.
findings.consequence: Tiny color-only marks offer little social personality and limited distance recognition; color distinction is not a substitute for names.
findings.recommendation: Explore expressive stable avatars/shapes with name pairing, multi-mode contrast and restrained motion; preserve attribution and do not make account photos mandatory.
findings.verify: Main: inspect 8 players on stage, both color modes and color-vision simulation; verify names remain primary and identical across phases.

findings.observation: A crown denotes the host in the lobby and the room-favorite poem in recap.
findings.consequence: The same symbol mixes authority and celebration, particularly if new directions make it the dominant motif.
findings.recommendation: Give host role and favorite celebration distinct visual grammars or clear contextual labels; do not add a new ranking system.
findings.verify: Main: compare roster and recap recognition without explanatory copy from the design author.

findings.observation: Archive uses optimistic local favorite state with silent rollback; reveal HeartButton uses reactive query state and logs failure; detail invokes mutation through a plain icon button. Only HeartButton has aria-pressed.
findings.consequence: One action has inconsistent pending/error/pressed feedback, making reliability hard to read and reducing accessibility consistency.
findings.recommendation: Unify observable favorite semantics and clear recovery feedback within the chosen design; use reversible positive acknowledgment, not a new scoring action.
findings.verify: Main: favorite/unfavorite across archive, detail and reveal, then inspect local failure and keyboard/screen-reader state without external writes.

findings.observation: PoemCard wraps an article in a Link but nests favorite and public-revoke buttons inside it; hover reveals arrow/line-count details through mouse-only state.
findings.consequence: Nested interactive elements and hover-only detail complicate touch/keyboard intent and may make accidental navigation more likely.
findings.recommendation: Define a clear primary read target and separate named utility targets, with equivalent focus/touch information and a 44px floor where actions matter.
findings.verify: Main: keyboard Tab/Enter/Space, touch favorite/revoke, and click card text; inspect focus order and whether one action unexpectedly navigates.

findings.observation: Four vertical stats precede a preservation/reveal info strip and featured-first gallery; favorite sort promotes one poem and uses larger card treatment, while each card repeats silhouette/count/coauthors/dots/date.
findings.consequence: Collection browsing can give inventory metadata more weight than poetry and obscure why a card is featured; source does not prove a user-visible layout failure.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether the collection is primarily reading, memories or saved favorites, and organize existing data accordingly. Do not add filters/search simply because an unused filtered empty state exists.
findings.verify: Main: inspect empty, one-poem and many-poem archives for guest/account, favorites and long previews in every responsive grid.

findings.observation: Each line reserves a number gutter plus 2.75rem author gutter; author names are absolutely positioned below the line, shown for only 2s. Archive also has full contributor legend and first-line teaser before full text.
findings.consequence: Fixed gutters reduce narrow reading width; transient names can overlap next lines or be missed, and duplicate teaser/full first line can dilute the artifact.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize an uninterrupted whole poem, with accessible persistent-on-request authorship and compact contextual identity. Preserve every human contributor, not the current margin construction.
findings.verify: Main: view all nine lines with maximum practical human content, select first/last author markers, use keyboard and screen reader, and inspect 320px plus zoom.

findings.observation: Public outsider detail suppresses favorite/revoke but PoemDisplay still renders Share and Save image; those handlers use participant share mutations and participant POST card access.
findings.consequence: A public reader can see actions whose backend authority differs from their access, leading to confusing failures or misleading public-consent language.
findings.recommendation: Make displayed capabilities and privacy copy match actual viewer role without weakening backend access. Distinguish copying an already-public link from granting publication if the selected implementation supports that existing authority boundary.
findings.verify: Main: open locally opted-in public poem as a fresh outsider, exercise visible controls and cancellation, and record actual errors/permissions before proposing workflow changes.

findings.observation: Poem sharing prepares an inert URL, delivers it, then activates; cancel/error rolls back. Whole-set sharing uses a distinct publish-after-delivery path. UI names are short Share versus Share the whole set with privacy copy nearby.
findings.consequence: A broad visual redesign can accidentally merge private save, public poem and public recap, or fabricate app dialogs that do not exist.
findings.recommendation: Treat one-poem public link, full-set public link and private image save as clearly different scopes; preserve native share cancellation and activation ordering.
findings.verify: Main: native share success/cancel/error, clipboard success/failure, pending-expired link and revoke, all local; no remote publication checks.

findings.observation: Full-card height grows by line count at 64px per line rather than measured wrapping; 38px line text and complete author attribution can exceed assumed height. Recap social card is fixed 630px high with multiple poem previews.
findings.consequence: Long human lines or many long names can pressure export bounds even if the in-app poem scrolls correctly; generated artwork needs its own evidence.
findings.recommendation: Prototype complete artifacts with worst-practical lines/names and preserve all attribution; explicitly separate fixed teaser truncation from full-text keepsake behavior.
findings.verify: Main: generate local full PNG in both modes and 8-poem recap preview, inspect pixels and print preview; no claim of current clipping without rendered output.

findings.observation: Print CSS sets white/black variables and avoids breaks within recap poem articles; callsites hide artifact actions and recap footer, but shared Header/Footer do not specify print:hidden.
findings.consequence: Unexpected site chrome or inline root theme precedence could reduce printed artifact quality; source alone does not establish the resulting print output.
findings.recommendation: Give single-poem and whole-set print clear artifact boundaries and ensure chrome, texture and color-mode residue are excluded without removing human attribution.
findings.verify: Main: inspect browser print preview from both dark and light poem/recap pages with multi-page content.

findings.observation: Site/poem/recap artwork use related but separate compositions; poem preview metadata says linejam.com while full-card metadata says linejam.app; manifest colors stay white.
findings.consequence: A new identity can drift across installed icon, live interface and shared artifact if only UI tokens change.
findings.recommendation: Design logo/wordmark, icons, social teaser, full keepsake, print and manifest as a coordinated system; resolve canonical naming/domain with site configuration in the final implementation.
findings.verify: Main: inspect actual icon pixels, installation/browser theme, all three generated preview types and full export; inventory did not inspect binary pixels.

findings.observation: Help traps Tab and locks body scroll but does not restore previous focus or bound panel height. StageShell is a fixed section with Exit but no Escape handler/focus trap; PoemDisplay focuses a heading but has no modal trap.
findings.consequence: Long text, small heights and keyboard navigation may expose content behind overlays or make exit hard; current visual quality cannot be inferred from aria labels alone.
findings.recommendation: Define a consistent appropriate overlay/nonmodal lifecycle: entry focus, reachable close, contained scrolling, background interaction policy and return focus. Respect the task rather than label every surface a modal blindly.
findings.verify: Main: keyboard-only open/close/Tab/Escape and mobile zoom on help, presentation and poem reading; inspect actual focus restoration and background reachability.

findings.observation: The QR popover is under the room-code branch, outside menuRef, while the open-popover mousedown handler closes all panels when the target is outside menuRef.
findings.consequence: [INFERENCE] Clicking inside QR/copy content may be treated as an outside click before its control fires; this needs a concrete rendered interaction.
findings.recommendation: Make popover containment and dismissal logic match the actual visual owner during implementation; prioritize reliable copy/close controls over decorative panel motion.
findings.verify: Main: open QR, click Copy code, retry error, and Close QR using mouse/touch/keyboard in the real local room surface.

findings.observation: Deployment update is fixed top z120, connection is top z60, room chrome is sticky z40, and draft retry error sits in writing content; each can carry a separate action/message.
findings.consequence: Simultaneous interruption states can cover controls or overload the same screen with competing recovery instructions.
findings.recommendation: Design explicit priority and placement for update/offline/draft error while preserving each real state; one message must not falsely imply successful persistence.
findings.verify: Main: locally combine stale deployment, offline, long submit error and keyboard-open writer; inspect accessible order and unobscured action area.

findings.observation: GlobalError replaces html/body yet uses runtime CSS variables normally set by RootLayout; error/not-found surfaces use fixed overflow-hidden layouts, blur and large display type; 404 reaches 10/14rem.
findings.consequence: Root failure before token initialization and short/zoomed viewports may compromise the very controls needed for recovery.
findings.recommendation: Design emergency states that remain readable without healthy app providers and let text/actions scroll; minimize decorative burden in repair states without losing brand recognition.
findings.verify: Main: render actual root/route failure and unknown path in controlled local QA, including first paint, 200% text and short landscape.

findings.observation: Loading appears as poetic dot, raw Loading text, skeletons and spinner. Route Error refers to current round even for other routes; recap fetch failure collapses to notFound.
findings.consequence: Different failure causes can feel inconsistent or misleading; loading’s theatrical tone should not obscure a stalled connection.
findings.recommendation: Create one coherent state vocabulary with task-specific cause/action and access-safe unavailable messaging; preserve privacy and distinguish loading, permission and transport recovery where actual data allows.
findings.verify: Main: inspect auth loading, join Suspense, private/public poem pending, recap backend failure and non-game route error.

findings.observation: Several independent loops/staggers and fade-ups exist, while type/breathe/final-line animations are defined but unmounted and AuthShowcase has delay without animation. Whole-poem reveal currently has no per-line animation.
findings.consequence: This source split plausibly contributes to operator reports of awkward or missing motion; dead definitions are not proof of rendered delight.
findings.recommendation: Specify a short motion score per meaningful event and remove unneeded loops/unused definitions only in the final selected implementation. Keep full poem visible together unless mechanics authority explicitly changes.
findings.verify: Main: record real transitions and compare timings with source triggers; test default and reduced motion, not just still screenshots.

findings.observation: Global reduced-motion overrides duration/iterations but not animation-delay; cards/bars may start opacity-zero and stamps use backwards fill. Hover/active transforms also remain with nearly instant transitions.
findings.consequence: Reduced-motion users may still wait through invisible stagger delays or see abrupt scale changes; no rendered invisibility claim is made here.
findings.recommendation: Design genuine static equivalents that remove unnecessary delay and preserve final-state visibility, not merely extremely short animations.
findings.verify: Main: reload populated archive/lobby in reduced motion, hover cards, press controls and inspect visibility/focus at initial and delayed frames.

findings.observation: Only crown calls punctuate; line/final-line tones are unused. Mute defaults off and gates vibration too; prefers-reduced-motion also disables audio/haptic. New AudioContext per tone may encounter autoplay policies.
findings.consequence: Visible sound toggles can promise more audible feedback than currently exists, while sensitivity preferences combine distinct sensory choices.
findings.recommendation: Define which existing milestones deserve optional sound/haptic; make silent and reduced-motion experiences complete, with explicit user control and no added gameplay dependency.
findings.verify: Main: use actual browser/device audio and vibration capability to inspect crown and mute; do not claim line/submission sound plays from unused hook definitions.

findings.observation: Leader ID change triggers crown tone, but crown/heart-burst markup keeps its React position without a leader key.
findings.consequence: [INFERENCE] A late favorite change can replay audio without the same visual settling effect, making sensory response inconsistent.
findings.recommendation: Treat leader change as one coherent optional feedback event and preserve a clear static favorite label; avoid excessive competitive celebration.
findings.verify: Main: change favorite leader with local players after recap mounts and compare visual animation, sound, text and reduced-motion behavior.

findings.area: Account surfaces and truthful local QA
findings.observation: Local integration provides a real account-disconnected surface; connected mode uses Clerk forms and account UI. Archive guest strip still describes optional cross-device signup and links to signup.
findings.consequence: Local-only visual QA cannot claim to have exercised real account/OTP/social flows; optional upgrade messaging must remain understandable when accounts are unavailable.
findings.recommendation: Cover truthful local fallback now and specify real connected provider surfaces as separately verified variants. Never mock successful sign-in or weaken credential/privacy gates to obtain screenshots.
findings.verify: Main: capture local sign-in/sign-up/callback/profile and inspect archive→signup fallback; connected account evidence requires separately authorized runtime capability.

findings.observation: Releases uses very large headings, long 96px article/title gaps, duplicated version header/inline version and collapsed technical detail. Feed links point to version fragments while ReleaseCard does not set an id in inspected source.
findings.consequence: Support reading may feel sparse/long despite dense technical detail; feed navigation may not land at its intended release.
findings.recommendation: Make update prose primary, de-emphasize redundant version data and retain useful collapsible technical content; align link destinations in final implementation.
findings.verify: Main: inspect populated/empty release page, expanded details and RSS entry navigation locally.

findings.observation: RootLayout wraps children in main; several child pages/phase bodies create their own main. Label defaults to p rather than a form-label element.
findings.consequence: Semantic hierarchy can diverge from visual hierarchy even if headings look polished.
findings.recommendation: Keep a deliberate single main landmark per ordinary document and real label/control associations; redesign composition semantics alongside style.
findings.verify: Main: inspect accessibility tree and heading/landmark navigation for home, room, recap and auth forms.

findings.observation: Inventory covers every actual user-facing page, component and generated artifact located in app/components plus scoped hooks/design/colorMode. API health/guest/deployment/internal drill and robots/sitemap are infrastructure or crawler endpoints, not human UI views; their observable auth/deployment errors are linked to real UI owners. Thin route/re-export/provider wrappers are linked, not duplicated.
findings.consequence: Fake components or fabricated dialogs would give five design builders false surface obligations; source findings alone do not establish actual pixels.
findings.recommendation: Use stable IDs as coverage checklist, include unused exported visual variants as explicit specimens/retirement decisions, and attach rendered evidence separately.
findings.verify: Main: perform rendered QA and final schema/coverage validation; this agent intentionally ran no builds, tests, formatters, services or browser sessions.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Use one family of compact name-first entry compositions for Host and Join, with room code revealed/preloaded only where needed; keep both current routes and immediate guest play.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: Improves continuity and keyboard ergonomics, but too much visual similarity can obscure whether the user is creating or joining; retain clear action verbs and invite context.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Let one dominant room code/QR/invite composition carry lobby invitation, with player names and minimum-two readiness immediately adjacent; move duplicate utility metadata into the existing tools disclosure.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: Reduces repeated chrome without sacrificing onboarding; needs distinct host and participant priorities and a clear route to presentation mode.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Explore an expressive responsive roster whose stable avatar/name pairs celebrate arrivals and distinguish writing, ready, away and watching without using several dimming/strike-through layers.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: More social warmth and recognizability, but every direction must keep long names, 8-player density, color-vision accessibility and assistive labels readable.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Unify carried context, editable line and exact-word constraint in a single compact task group; keep the submit action reachable in an in-flow tray and reduce desktop empty textarea height for short rounds.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: Improves hand/eye travel and short-round proportionality, but cannot obscure the one carried line, current target or draft recovery; actual keyboard proof is required.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Replace continuous ready-state decoration with a brief response when the target becomes valid and a clear static enabled Submit state; give confirmed persistence one satisfying acknowledgment before existing waiting handoff.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: Quieter and more causal, but reduced-motion users still need the same static readiness/persistence evidence and rapid server advance may shorten acknowledgment.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: After submission, lead with a positive personal completion state and one readable group-progress representation; keep names, away/watch distinctions, soft pacing and host end-game access secondary but discoverable.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: Reduces redundant progress signals and avoids crossing out contributors; must not invent side games, auto-submissions or remove visibility into the actual blocker.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Make the whole human poem the center of the ceremony with clear reader attribution and one dominant return/continue control; use shared labels that describe actual revealed/assigned state rather than claiming a synchronized read-finished state.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: Stronger read-aloud focus, but the existing local Done/Finish actions are not a server-wide reading protocol; no line-by-line reveal mechanics should be introduced.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Surface the existing complete-set recap as a clear phase conclusion, with replay/favorite recognition and the next social choice grouped ahead of optional publishing utilities.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: May require rearranging rather than appending the existing recap composition; preserve any-participant rematch, Back to Lobby and Exit as genuinely different actions.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Group Print/Save image as private keeping and Share poem/Share whole set as public publication, with explicit scope and current viewer capability before the native share sheet.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: Clearer consent but an extra disclosure can add friction; never merge private download with public enablement or publish on native cancellation.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Give poem previews and contributor context priority over statistics and repeated miniature metadata, using favorites as an understandable sort/treatment rather than unexplained oversized first-card decoration.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: Warmer collection browsing, but sparse poetry can look uniform; use actual content and existing metadata without adding search/filter product mechanics solely for variety.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Give late arrivals a clear spectator identity and current-phase context, plus a concise statement that they join the next existing game; carry their name/avatar through waiting and reveal.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: Preserves inclusion without breaking active assignment fairness, but cannot reveal hidden lines or add spectator participation to current-round completion.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Keep guest archive and local identity fully accessible; place optional account preservation explanations near the existing save/return context and show truthful account-disconnected local fallback.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: Supports guest trust without conversion pressure; connected-account design needs separately authorized evidence and cannot promise cloud persistence in local mode.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Give help, appearance, QR and account utilities a coherent family of nonmodal/popover or modal patterns chosen by task, with explicit keyboard entry/exit, focus restoration and bounded scrolling.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: A uniform aesthetic helps, but making everything modal creates unnecessary friction; preserve the actual share/print OS surfaces instead of pretending they are custom panels.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Arrange offline, draft-submit failure and deployment-update information by urgency so the highest actionable state is visible without erasing the others; explain what is saved and what needs retry/reload.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: Reduces recovery noise, but aggregation cannot hide uncertainty or claim successful submission; local fault scenarios must prove the selected hierarchy.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Use brief optional sound/haptic only for carefully selected existing milestones such as confirmed action or favorite recognition, paired with complete visual/textual state and a discoverable mute preference.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: Adds delight without mechanics, but autoplay/device support and sensitivity vary; every design must remain fully legible silent and reduced-motion.

workflowAlternatives.proposal: Design site preview, one-poem public teaser, access-safe fallback, full attributed PNG, public recap, print and device icons as one recognizable family with formats sized for their actual destination.
workflowAlternatives.tradeoff: More complete identity than token recoloring, but generated images require separate font/layout/pagination evidence and must preserve privacy and all human attribution.
